summary.headline: FY26 total income rose 85% to Rs 57.62 crore and PAT to Rs 2.44 crore, but H2 margins fell on rupee-driven input costs, depreciation and marketing spend.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 total income of Rs 57.62 crore (up 85% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 6.31 crore (up 48.34%) and PAT of Rs 2.44 crore (up 14.76%). Capacity utilisation at the Changodar plant rose to roughly 2,500-3,000 MTPA from about 1,200 MTPA previously, against 4,800 MTPA installed. H2 PAT and margins were lower than H1, which management attributed to rupee depreciation (about 84-85 to 93-94 per USD) flowing through average-cost inventory, about Rs 1.5 crore of extra depreciation, higher working-capital interest, and D2C marketing and SKU expansion (24 SKUs versus 3 last year). Management also said H2 sales were weaker because most of the festive selling was completed before Diwali.

financial_highlights.change: from around Rs 5 crore last year

segments.name: B2B cashew processing
segments.commentary: Core business; capacity utilisation of 2,500-3,000 MTPA in FY26 against 4,800 MTPA installed. Management says FY26 volume growth was the sole driver of revenue growth, with no price or mix contribution.

segments.name: B2C / D2C (DriFrutz brand)
segments.commentary: Revenue to date is very small, around Rs 50-60 lakh including gifting. Target is 10% of total revenue, with timing unclear (six months to a couple of years). Listed on Amazon, Flipkart, DriFrutz website and Hyperpure; Blinkit in discussion.

segments.name: By-products (shell, husk)
segments.commentary: About 70% of raw cashew comes out as shell, sold directly to CNSL processors, and about 2-2.5% as husk, also sold. No CNSL or pellet processing is done in-house.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capacity utilisation target of 3,500-4,000 MTPA; FY28 target of 4,500-5,000 MTPA.
EBITDA margin target of 12-15%; implied PAT margin of roughly 5-7% per management.
B2C target of 10% of revenue in FY27, with timing uncertain.
Management targets a 40-45% revenue CAGR over the next three years.
Debt-to-equity to peak at about 0.6 by year-end and stay below 1:1; management aims to fund further growth through debt rather than equity for now.
Management expects about one more month to pass through the rupee-driven cost increases before pricing is fully absorbed; a 15-20 day Diwali production break is expected in H2.
capex_capacity: Changodar plant installed capacity 4,800 MTPA; utilisation about 2,500-3,000 MTPA in FY26.
Automation at about 80% across the seven processing stages (deshelling, boiling, moisture control, peeling, colour sorting).
Management aims for 300-400 tonnes per month of deshelling output in the first six months of FY27 and said about 1,800 tonnes of capacity is still unused.
Working-capital bank facility raised last year; the company plans to reach full utilisation by year-end without further debt raising.
demand_pricing: Raw cashew cost rose from about Rs 110-120/kg a couple of years ago to Rs 140-150 last year and about Rs 170-175 now.
Rupee moved from about 84-85 to 93-94 per USD by March 2026. Average-cost inventory accounting carried this into COGS in H2.
Fuel price rises are raising transport costs; the company is still absorbing the cost increases.
Sourcing shifted from West Africa to Tanzania and Ghana in Dec-Feb; local Indian crop is priced higher.
Management says the market is softer from February, and a large part of the festive sales is done about 10 days before Diwali.
Management says big established brands are not yet direct competitors; it cited quick commerce growth and positive packaging feedback from Blinkit.
Hyperpure takes a 15-20% margin; Blinkit listing is still in discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 margins and PAT fall versus H1, and why was H2 revenue weaker?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a roughly Rs 1.5 crore depreciation hit, rupee depreciation from 84-85 to 93-94 flowing through average-cost inventory, higher interest on newly drawn working capital, and D2C marketing and SKU expansion. Most festive sales were done before Diwali, and the market weakened from February.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA and PAT margins should be expected going forward, and what is the war impact on imported raw material?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA target is 12-15%, with PAT around 5-7%. The rupee move and higher fuel costs are being absorbed gradually; management expects about one month more before pricing catches up fully, and flagged that retail spending will weigh on profit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the B2B and B2C revenue split and the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: B2C plus gifting is very small, around Rs 50-60 lakh to date. The first target is 10% of revenue, and the timeline ranges from six months to a couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory build-up and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: About 25-30% of stock is cashew with testa residue that needs manual cleaning. This is sent to home-based labour, which has grown from about 30 to around 80 workers. Borrowings rose from about Rs 5 crore to over Rs 10 crore on working-capital needs from higher raw-material prices and capacity. Peak D/E is expected at about 0.6, below 1:1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sourcing mix and the by-product outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 raw cashew was sourced mainly from West and East Africa, then Tanzania and Ghana. Shell is about 70% of raw cashew input and husk about 2-2.5%, both sold rather than processed; these ratios are expected to hold at higher volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What are the channel economics, CAC and competitive positioning in D2C?
qa_highlights.answer: No CAC has been calculated yet; Hyperpure and Amazon marketing is funded from the marketing budget. Management does not see established brands as direct competitors yet and is focused on positioning DriFrutz in the premium segment.

risks_watch: Gross and EBITDA margins are under pressure from rupee depreciation, average-cost inventory accounting, and fuel-driven transport costs. Watch whether the 12-15% EBITDA target holds in H1 FY27.
Inventory of around Rs 18 crore, including roughly 25-30% of stock that needs manual deshelling, is a working-capital and dead-stock risk.
Borrowings have roughly doubled to over Rs 10 crore and finance cost rose to Rs 1.3 crore from Rs 0.48 crore; peak D/E target is about 0.6.
B2C scale-up depends on quick commerce and gifting, which are still at very small revenue levels. The 10% target has no firm timeline.
Raw cashew prices are rising every year, and sourcing depends mainly on African origins.

The call had audio interruptions, and several answers were loosely framed. Management also gave unclear answers on the timing of the 2027 product update and the date for reaching the utilisation targets.
summary.management_tone: Confident on scale-up and the long-term FMCG strategy, but cautious on near-term margins, which management tied to currency, fuel and the weak post-Diwali market. Answers on the timing of targets such as B2C share and utilisation were vague.
key_quotes: We are structurally positioning ourselves to target 40 to 45% CAGR over the next three years while delivering sustainable high-margin growth.
So EBITDA will be somewhere around 12 to 15% you can consider that.
So we are focusing more on a EBITDA side rather actually looking directly on PAT margins.
Right now B2C segment is very less.
